# The lane contract

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit. Source: config/lane-contract.json.
     Regenerate with `python3 scripts/lane_contract.py render`. -->

Per lane: the entrance condition, the exit condition, the permitted writers, and the evidence that justifies occupancy. This document is rendered from the same file the guard, the sweep and the integration harness read, so it cannot drift from the enforcement.

Wave phase reached: **2** — the lane contract asserted by the harness. A clause marked **live** is asserted by the harness on every trunk commit. A clause marked **promised** is skipped until its phase ships, and fails the harness the moment its phase has passed with nothing enforcing it.

## The flow

| # | Lane | Segment | Stall window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Intake | planning | — |
| 2 | Planning | planning | 120 min |
| 3 | Green Light | planning | — |
| 4 | Backlog | work | — |
| 5 | Todo | work | 15 min |
| 6 | Hand-work | work | — |
| 7 | In Progress | work | 60 min |
| 8 | In Review | work | 120 min |
| 9 | Done | work | — |

Planning exit is the transition **Green Light → Backlog** — where the second critic writes its verdict, and the boundary the guard's scope is derived from.

## Off the flow

| Lane | Why it is off the flow |
| --- | --- |
| Triage | the guard's own destination for a card returned three times — policing it would bounce the sink straight back to Intake and loop |
| Canceled | terminal and off the path; the card makes no claim to justify |
| Duplicate | terminal and off the path; the card makes no claim to justify |

## The lanes

### Intake

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | Every writer that creates work writes here first — the relay, the planner, a mid-epic discovery, a human. There is no other valid first lane.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2680 points every writer at Intake._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | A classification exists: one-off, epic, or roll-up. There are exactly THREE ways out. Two are an approval the CEO gives. For a card nobody filed under an epic the way out is the groomer — it proposes a batch, the CEO approves it in Green Light, and the approved batch drains to Planning (groomer.py drain) — the drain moves what the free planner slots take, and every other card of the batch is QUEUED (DRE-5435): it stays here under the `groom-queued` label, listed in the `groom-queued` record on the groomer's standing card, and the bureau-pipeline sweep moves it to Planning one card per free slot, oldest batch first. One approval moves the whole batch; a queued card is never proposed again, and waiting in the queue is never escalated. For a card whose PARENT EPIC is being planned the way out is adoption (DRE-4668, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-23): the planning exit writes the child's routing verdict and moves it to Backlog, where it waits — the epic's own green light is the approval for the cards filed under it, and nothing builds until the CEO moves that epic to In Progress. A child the verdict sends back to Planning is not adopted and stays here. The third is the Urgent fast path (DRE-4150, on point 2 of the same signed answer of 2026-09-17): the sweep moves a card to Planning on its next pass when it is not an epic, is at Urgent and was RAISED to Urgent (or created at it) after the rule's ship moment in config/urgent-fast-path.json — read off the card's own Linear history, never its label — carries no signed exclusion from the CEO on the groomer's standing card, and has no parent epic or one that is In Progress. At most three a sweep across the whole fleet, oldest raised first, counted off the receipts already posted on the board so two repos sweeping in the same minute move three between them; the rest wait for the next sweep and the run log names them. INTAKE_HOLD does not stop it — the hold pauses the groomer's drain, and an Urgent card waiting behind a pause is the opposite of the rule. The card carries a receipt naming the rule, posted just before the move; the move is read back off the card's lane, and a card whose move did not land is tried again on a later sweep, at most three attempts in all, before it is left to the groomer. A card that reached Planning is never moved by this rule again. Urgency skips the queue, not Planning's classifier and critic. AGE IS NOT AN EXIT: no card is moved out of this lane for being old, this lane carries no stall window, and there is no window of any length in its place (DRE-4141, on the CEO's signed answer of 2026-09-17). The sweep reports how many cards are waiting and how old the oldest is, and moves none of them for their age. BLOCKING WORK IS NOT AN EXIT EITHER (DRE-4152, on point 4 of the same signed answer): when an Intake card is a `blockedBy` relation of a card in Todo, In Progress or In Review, or of a Backlog child of an In Progress epic, the sweep of the blocked card's repo says so once per pair, in plain English, on the blocked card's epic — or on the blocked card when it has none — naming both cards and the two ways a person can send the blocker on: raise it to Urgent, or approve it in the next groom batch. It moves no card, applies no label and files nothing in Triage or Green Light, and its run log lists every pair each pass. | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | Anything that creates a card, and the retroactive pass that moves the legacy Backlog in. ONE of them also moves a card onward, and only with an approval behind it: plan.yml adopts a planned epic's own children into Backlog (DRE-4668). The groomer's drain — the other way out — writes Planning rather than this lane, so it is named as a writer there.  
Permitted writers: `relay`, `plan.yml`, `mid_epic.py`, `linear_ops.py`, `backlog_cutover.py`, `operator` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | The card exists and carries no classification yet. | Phase 5 — promised |

### Planning

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | The card has been classified as needing a plan. | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | The card leaves by the route its shape declares (DRE-2844): a one-off the check can route goes straight to the build queue, carrying the routing verdict its own card decided and owing no plan artifact and no green light — a one-off whose card names no exit condition to route on, and whose labels and title do not route it, goes to the planner's rewrite before the critic's word is read (DRE-6380), and takes the escalation exit below only when the card could not be read (DRE-3038). A one-off is READ BEFORE IT MOVES (DRE-3041): the same pre-approval critic an epic gets, one bounded call between the shape stamp and the move, asking whether this is one pull request of work an agent can build unattended with nothing in it that is a decision. A pass moves the card, because nothing reads a one-off after this point — and so does a declaration: a one-off whose explicit role label routes it to a person is moved on that label and never read by the critic, because that precedence asks no model (DRE-5805). Each other answer goes to whoever can act on it (DRE-5376): a SEND_BACK — a defect in the card an agent can fix from the repository and the card alone — is answered by the planner, which revises the card in place while it stays in this lane and posts what it changed per finding, and the critic reads it again on a fresh planning run; a one-off sent back `MAX_ROUNDS` times leaves for Triage with every finding named, never for the CEO's queue. A QUESTION — a decision only the CEO can make, whether the critic or the revising planner asks it — and a critic that could not run take the escalation exit below. A critic QUESTION whose finding names card text is read as a revision and answered by the planner's rewrite, and a QUESTION whose finding is a decision, or that the classifier cannot place, is the escalation (DRE-6359). An epic leaves for the CEO on a plan artifact, and for an epic it is still no artifact, no exit; a roll-up leaves as child epics under itself, each sent to Planning to be planned on its own. A card carrying no shape is CLASSIFIED by the run before it routes (DRE-3029) — one bounded read of the card against the three shapes, stamped with who made the call and on which model — so nothing sits here owing a stamp a person has to write by hand. An epic leaves for the CEO in Green Light only once BOTH critics have passed it on its current planning attempt (DRE-5268): a send-back at either critic is answered by the planner and re-read by that critic while the epic stays in this lane, and a plan that exhausts EITHER critic's round bound, or whose second critic produces no result twice, leaves for Triage with `needs-human` and the finding still open — never for the CEO's queue. Either bound, on either route, is first tried without a person before it parks anything (DRE-6452): the bound exit (`scripts/plan_bound.py`) reads the worst finding of every send-back round on the attempt, a decision-class finding goes to Green Light as one question, a revision-class set gets one more planner rewrite on a fresh attempt, once per card, and the park in Triage comes only after that. There is a fourth exit and it is the only one that is not a plan: the run ESCALATES, with a reason stated in business terms, and the card parks in Green Light (DRE-2848) — the classifier takes it for a card it cannot place, and the planner for an epic whose reasoning is itself the deliverable. A classifier call that came back with no classification at all, and failed the same way on its one retry, is NOT that escalation (DRE-5975): nothing has read the card, so there is no question for the CEO, and `planning_escalation.park_unread` parks it in Triage instead, its operator note opening with the stall exit's tag and no label — never in Green Light. Hand-planning is that escalation and nothing else — no label, flag or lane skips this lane, and the one sanctioned bypass past the Todo gate, `break-glass`, returns the card here for the classification it went round. The SWEEP's stall exit (DRE-4124) parks a card nothing has happened to in the lane's stall window in Triage, with its reason on it and no label: a card no planner and no critic has read is the operator's to move and not the CEO's (DRE-5268), and a card nobody can move belongs in the queue of the person who can, rather than labeled `needs-human` and left sitting here — which is what froze thirteen cards, the oldest for thirty-five days. A card waiting in the planner line is not stalled (DRE-5177): under the fleet-wide planner cap it is served in line order, and the sweep escalates it to Triage only when its wait passes the bound in `config/planner-queue.json`. Nor is a card waiting on a limit death (DRE-5841): the limit recovery re-enters it once the marker's reset passes, so the stall exit leaves it until that reset plus the lane's stall window — or, for a marker that names no reset, until the marker's own time plus the window — and never in the pass the recovery re-entered or handed it off.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2720 writes the epic's artifact, DRE-2844 branches the exit on the shape and DRE-2848 adds the escalation exit; the gate that refuses an epic's exit without an artifact is Phase 5._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | The planner, the sweep that re-triggers it, a build run handing back a card that turned out to be an epic, a build run whose turn-cap death stopped before implementation green and is sent back to be cut smaller (the `replan` write, DRE-4366), a build run whose dead-run cap is reached on a silent death — no pull request and no blocker note — and the planner has not yet had the card on that budget, sent once to be split before anyone parks it (the same `replan` write, under the `✂️ dead-run-cap → Planning:` receipt, DRE-6178), the sweep's two no-PR dead-run caps — a card In Progress with no live run, or In Review with its pull request gone — making the same hand-off once on the same budget under the same receipt (DRE-6186), the groomer draining a batch the CEO approved, the sweep's Urgent fast path moving a card raised to Urgent after that rule shipped (DRE-4150), the critic's audit moving a card it could not classify, the guarded write layer every automated card-minting seam goes through — the Todo gate returning a card it cannot repair, the one-off producer, and the medic/watch seams that file a fresh card (DRE-2858) — and a human. And the hygiene agent, returning from Green Light a row that was never a decision — a planner that died, a classifier transport failure, a child without acceptance criteria, an escalation that asks for a split or an access, a stall park — with the cause named (DRE-5365). And the Hand-work migration, sending a code card from Hand-work that has had no critic pass back here to be read before anything builds it (DRE-6230). And the sweep, handing off a build agent's `nothing-to-change` blocker that attested fewer than every acceptance criterion — or a card with no criteria to attest against — to be re-read, once per card, under the resolver's receipt (DRE-6458): a second such note is a person's call, asked in Green Light.  
Permitted writers: `plan.yml`, `reconcile.py`, `agent-task.yml`, `groomer.py`, `critic_score.py`, `linear_ops.py`, `operator`, `hygiene.py`, `hand_work_migration.py` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | The plan artifact on the card: business case, KPIs as data, risk, outcome.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2720._ | Phase 5 — promised |

### Green Light

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | Six kinds of row, and no other (DRE-5268, DRE-4271, DRE-6414). (a) A plan arrives only after BOTH critics passed it on its current planning attempt — the evidence is a `plan-critic: stage=post … result=PASS` record on the epic. (b) The planner escalated a business question, in plain English with a recommendation, and stated why (DRE-2848): every escalation the plan route makes, the classifier's for a card it cannot place and the planner's for an epic whose reasoning is itself the deliverable, each stated in business terms or refused. A critic QUESTION whose finding names card text is read as a revision and answered by the planner's rewrite, and a QUESTION whose finding is a decision, or that the classifier cannot place, is the escalation (DRE-6359). On the one-off route that is the critic's QUESTION, or the revising planner's own, and a critic that decided nothing — never a card the critic sent back for a defect, which the planner revises (DRE-5376). The round bound, on the one-off route and on the epic route alike, reaches this lane by one door only: the bound exit (scripts/plan_bound.py, DRE-6415) reads the worst finding of every send-back round on the attempt, the one its marker records, before anything parks, and a decision-class finding among them arrives here as one question through this same writer, carrying the Finding, Question and Recommendation lines, when that question is in words the CEO reads; a bound with no such finding, or whose question the refusal would not show, grants the planner one more rewrite or parks in Triage, and is never a row here. (c) The fleet was at its cap of epics in motion when the CEO approved an epic, so the planner labeled it `epic-queued`, recorded the approval on the epic in the ⏸️ receipt of that same name stating the epic's place in line, and returned it here to wait in line for the sweep (DRE-5129) — proposed by the operator and accepted by the CEO's approval of DRE-5268; the row asks nothing of the CEO, it shows where his approved work is in the line. (d) A build in flight stopped on something only a person can settle: the build run's escalate-by-exception question (DRE-1655: ambiguous intent, a risky change, or a business A-vs-B decision the CEO should own, posted as a plain-English question), or the merge gate is holding a green, approved pull request for a required code-owner review and moved the card here to ask the person the repository's rules name (DRE-4341 — only when the calling repo's merge-gate stub wakes the gate on a submitted review, because the sweep dispatches nothing for a card in this lane). A proof run that meets a criterion only the CEO's own press can satisfy is the same kind (DRE-5925): it records every other row, opens the record's pull request, and parks the card here once, its question naming the press beside a 🔬 proof-waiting hold that keeps the dispatcher off the card. Each row of kinds (b) and (d) carries the declared Finding, Question and Recommendation lines, rendered by `scripts/console_escalation.py` (DRE-3893), with `none given` and the reason on the Recommendation line where the agent stated none, and an `escalation-choices` block after them where the writer produced one, whose recommended choice is the Recommendation's answer; `tests/test_green_light_writers_declare.py` holds every writer of the two kinds, and of kind (f) below, the discovery finds to that. Kind (d) predates DRE-5268 and stays its own kind, never read as (b): the agent stopped where it could not choose, and a review request asks a person to act rather than to settle a business question. (e) The console filed the week's agent-failure report as one `no-code` card for the CEO to read (DRE-4271) — proposed by the CEO's own decision of 2026-09-18 and accepted by his approval of DRE-4271; the row asks nothing of him but to read it and close it. It is neither a question nor a plan nor a defect, so no sweep or keeper moves it, re-sends it to Planning or closes it, its lack of acceptance criteria is not a thing to fix, and only the CEO closes it. A row of this kind is recognized by its title `What broke the agents — week ending <Saturday> (PT)`, its `no-code` label and its description's first line, which opens `Weekly agent report — Green Light kind weekly-report`. Its write site lives in agent-bureau (`console/backend/weekly_agent_report_card.py`, DRE-5020), outside this repository, so it has no `arrivals` record. (f) The sweep's question about an epic that grew past the size the CEO approved (DRE-6414): when an epic in motion runs more than `config/epic-growth.json`'s `ratio` times the size he approved and at least its `minimum_added` more cards, the sweep creates one `no-code` card of its own here, with no parent and no `agent:*` role, asked once per crossing while the epic keeps running — the epic itself never comes to this lane, because a Green Light epic promotes no children. Its description is the declared Finding, Question and Recommendation lines and nothing else, with no `escalation-choices` block: he answers in his signed words, `re-approve` or `split`, and the sweep settles it, closing the card `Done` on either answer — a split also files a mid-epic amendment that sends the epic to Planning — and recording a card that leaves this lane unanswered as withdrawn. A row of this kind is recognized by its title `Epic grew past its green light: DRE-<n> — approved at <N> cards, running <M>` and its `no-code` label. `arrivals` names every way a row is written into this lane from this repository, one record per site; `callers` on a record whose site is a Python function names the units permitted to reach it, because a write made through a function is attributed to its caller.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records — the six kinds exist, nothing yet reads a card's arrival against them._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | The CEO answers: an approved plan activates and its children promote through the dependency gate, with no review after the approval — both critics read it before it arrived here (DRE-5268) — an answered escalation returns to Todo, a rejected one goes to Backlog. A proof card parked here leaves on the CEO's signed answer, carried back to Hand-work by the proof run that his answer re-dispatches (DRE-5925). A queued epic is started by the sweep when the count of epics in motion falls under the cap, the highest Linear Priority first and the oldest approval on a tie, by moving it to In Progress, which fires the same activate route the CEO's own approval does; an epic already in motion that is re-approved after a mid-epic amendment starts past the cap rather than waiting; and an epic that leaves this lane any other way (re-planned after an amendment, handed back to Planning for a review it missed, parked, canceled) has left the line and loses the `epic-queued` label, so a re-planned epic arriving here again waits for a fresh approval (DRE-5129). Or the hygiene agent sends a row back to Planning that was never a decision, with the cause named; it never approves, and a real question stays here (DRE-5365). A growth question leaves when the sweep closes it `Done` on the CEO's signed `re-approve` or `split`, or when it is moved out unanswered, which the sweep records as withdrawn and moves nothing (DRE-6414).  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | The planner, the two agent runs that escalate, the proof run parking a card on a press only the CEO can make (DRE-5925), the merge gate parking a card whose pull request waits on a required code-owner review (DRE-4341), a human, the console filing the week's agent-failure report (DRE-4271), and the sweep asking about an epic that grew past the size the CEO approved (DRE-6414).  
Permitted writers: `plan.yml`, `agent-task.yml`, `agent-fix.yml`, `merge-gate.yml`, `proof-task.yml`, `reconcile.py`, `operator`, `console` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | A plan artifact with the `plan-critic: stage=post … result=PASS` record both critics' passes end in (DRE-5268), an escalation comment written in business terms — never code, never a diff — the merge gate's code-owner hold comment naming who must review which folders (DRE-4341), or, for a kind-(e) row, the report card itself — titled `What broke the agents — week ending <Saturday> (PT)`, carrying `no-code`, its description opening `Weekly agent report — Green Light kind weekly-report` (DRE-4271) — or, for a kind-(f) row, the question card itself — titled `Epic grew past its green light: DRE-<n> — approved at <N> cards, running <M>`, carrying `no-code`, its description the three lines: Finding, Question and Recommendation (DRE-6414).  
_Waiting on: needs routing verdicts (DRE-2724) writing on every card before arrival can be judged against the evidence._ | Phase 5 — promised |

### Backlog

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | It carries a routing verdict — one of the five in config/routing-verdicts.json, machine-readable on the card.  
_Waiting on: the vocabulary exists (DRE-2724); what is still missing is a writer that puts a verdict on EVERY card at planning exit — DRE-2721's second critic._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | The verdict's destination is reached, and the sweep is what reaches it (DRE-3385). Which verdict lands where is config/routing-verdicts.json's to say, and the sweep reads that file, never this sentence. It promotes a FLEET card to Todo once the dependency gate clears, the WIP cap has room and — for a child of an epic — both critics passed the plan on its current planning attempt before the green light (DRE-3059, DRE-5268). The sweep promotes a WORKBENCH or OPERATOR card to its verdict's destination on the same gates too, stamping the marks its verdict declares — `operator-step` and `no-code` for OPERATOR, none for WORKBENCH — before the move, so the card never sits there missing one; it never stamps `hand-built`, which is the CEO's mark, applied only when he asks for it, and nothing automatic applies it (2026-10-07, DRE-6227); nothing is dispatched for it, it takes no slot under the WIP cap, and the receipt says whose turn it is. Under DRE-5240 that destination is Hand-work, the lane where a person's work waits, and FLEET alone goes to Todo (DRE-5321, DRE-5322). An epic here whose children are all closed, with at least one Done, is closed by the sweep, with the same receipt and the same advance of the epics it blocks as one in Todo, In Progress or In Review (DRE-6410); every child Canceled and none Done is not a completion, and it stays. A PARKED card does not leave, and is never reported as stalled; a NEEDS WORK card goes back to Planning, which is the planner's move and not the sweep's. A card carrying no verdict at all is not promoted, whether or not it has a parent epic: the epic's approval says the PLAN was approved, never who builds this piece of it. A verdict approves ONE trip through Planning (DRE-4962): a card that has entered Intake, Green Light, Triage, Canceled, Duplicate or Done since its newest verdict is not promoted — the sweep refuses it `stale-verdict`, says once on the card when the verdict was written, which of those lanes it passed through since and that it needs Planning again to be built, and leaves it here. A later exit from Planning, or for a child its epic's green light, is a fresh approval. Since DRE-4884 that exit retires, on the record, every verdict written before the card re-entered Planning, and stamps the one it reads now — taking off an `operator-step` the old verdict put on when the new one does not — so a re-planned card leaves with exactly one live verdict, and a retired one is read by nothing. The check reads the card's lane history, so it is the last gate, asked only of a card every other gate has passed; a history Linear cannot return holds the card that sweep and says nothing on it.  
_Waiting on: the sweep carries every verdict it promotes out of this lane and refuses the rest (DRE-2724, DRE-3385); asserting the transitions needs the history Phase 5 records; DRE-5240 pointed WORKBENCH and OPERATOR at Hand-work (DRE-5321) and the sweep carries them there (DRE-5322)._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | The planner and mid-epic discovery create here; the sweep and the dead-run cap park here; and the build run parks the card it could not build — a stated blocker, or a run that kept dying past the cap (DRE-2859) — on a silent death only after the planner has had the card once on that budget (DRE-6178). A person also lands a card here by sending it back from Green Light — the rejected answer that lane's exit names — or by moving it here by hand; that move approves nothing, and the `stale-verdict` refusal above is what keeps the sweep from building it (DRE-4962). And the hygiene agent, returning a Triage card whose mechanical defect it fixed — a prose blocker made true by the relation it added, a dependency loop a Done card already broke, a retired-repo card marked operator-step and parked — never to Todo (DRE-5365). And the Hand-work migration, returning a code card from Hand-work that has had a critic pass here carrying a fresh FLEET verdict, for the sweep to promote (DRE-6230).  
Permitted writers: `plan.yml`, `mid_epic.py`, `reconcile.py`, `dead_run.py`, `linear_ops.py`, `agent-task.yml`, `hygiene.py`, `hand_work_migration.py` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | A routing verdict comment; and, for a child of an epic, an epic that has passed Planning exit.  
_Waiting on: the marker exists and the sweep reads it (DRE-2724); asserting that every Backlog card carries one needs the writer at planning exit (DRE-2721)._ | Phase 5 — promised |

### Hand-work

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | A card enters on a WORKBENCH or OPERATOR routing verdict, the two whose actor is `operator` in config/routing-verdicts.json. The sweep moves it here, stamping the marks the verdict declares — `operator-step` and `no-code` for OPERATOR, none for WORKBENCH — before the move. It never stamps `hand-built`: that is the CEO's mark, applied only when he asks for it, and nothing automatic applies it (his rule of 2026-10-07, DRE-6227). Nothing is dispatched for it, it takes no slot under the WIP cap, it carries no stall window, and it is never reported as stalled by the run watchdog. But a person's card that has waited past `config/hand-work-age.json`'s hours gets one `hand-work-overdue` alarm for the operator, once per entry and from its own repo's sweep (DRE-6409) — except a standing card and the CEO's own `hand-built` card, which never alarm. An epic never enters.

### In Review

> Folded from the two review lanes DRE-2726 retired (DRE-2818 deleted their entries once Linear archived the states). Both meant 'a pull request is open and being checked'; the sweep now keys off the evidence — a verdict bound to the head — rather than off which of two lanes the card sat in.

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | A pull request is open on the card's branch and is being checked: by the critic, by the verifier, or by the merge gate. The card may arrive here from ANY pre-review lane — Intake, Triage, Planning, Backlog, Todo or In Progress — and not only from In Progress: a pull request opened outside the relay's dispatch has no agent-task run behind it to have written In Progress, so qa-review.yml advances the card itself when the pull request opens (DRE-4179) — or, for a draft, when it is marked ready for review: a draft is not being checked, and its card stays where it is (DRE-5801). Green Light is not a pre-review lane for this route: it is the CEO's own queue and a branch existing does not take a card out of it. The one move out of Green Light into this lane is the merge gate's release (DRE-4341): once the required code-owner review it was holding for has landed, it moves the card back here before it merges — only a card it parked itself, recognized by its own hold marker, never a card someone else put in Green Light. And there is one more move out of Green Light into this lane, only on a card the sweep parked there itself when the review lane's re-trigger budget was spent, recognized by its own `🔒 hold: reason=review-cap-spent` stamp standing unspent: the hygiene agent's holds lane returns it when the pull request has a new head. An Operator decision on that pull request moves the card nowhere by itself — it starts the fix agent once, and the fix that run pushes is the new head the holds lane returns the card on. The holds lane also returns a card from Triage when the fix loop's `fix-dispute` or `unfixable-check` hold on it lifts on a new head (DRE-6172). Not live yet: the sweep's `review-cap-spent` park lands with DRE-6181 and the holds lane's returns with DRE-6180 and DRE-6273; until then neither move is made. The sweep also carries a Backlog card here when it opens a ready pull request for a build agent's stamped `branch-without-pr` blocker, or finds one already open and ready for review, on the card's `agent/<card>-…` branch (DRE-6447): the stamp says the work is finished and only the pull request is missing, and the critic and the merge gate check that pull request like any other. The draft it opens for a legacy note of that class — a marker with no `class=`, which may describe a branch the agent held on purpose — moves the card nowhere, and the sweep asks in Green Light instead. Not live until the sweep's resolver (DRE-6508) and its call site (DRE-6448) land.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | GitHub merges the pull request and linear-sync writes Done — or the pull request is gone and the card is requeued under the dead-run cap. Or the hygiene agent closes a proof card whose merged record meets every criterion in its table, under the CEO's standing rule (DRE-5365).  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | The build run puts cards here; the critic, the gate, the fix run and the sweep move them on. The sweep also FILES a card straight into this lane for every dependabot pull request (DRE-3665): the pull request already exists and is already being checked, so there is nothing to plan or dispatch. And the hygiene agent, moving a proof card from Triage to the lane its already-open pull request says it is in (DRE-5365). And the proof run, after the CEO's answer, when it pushes the amended record to the pull request that was already open (DRE-5925). And the sweep again, for a Backlog card whose build agent wrote a stamped `branch-without-pr` blocker, when it opens the ready pull request for the work on the card's `agent/<card>-…` branch or finds one already open and ready for review (DRE-6447) — the draft it opens for a legacy note of that class moves no card.  
Permitted writers: `agent-task.yml`, `qa-review.yml`, `merge-gate.yml`, `agent-fix.yml`, `reconcile.py`, `hygiene.py`, `proof-task.yml` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | An open pull request; and, once the critic has run, a verdict bound to the head sha.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |

### Triage

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | The card itself is malformed and cannot proceed as written: an unroutable repo label, an archived repo, a card the readiness guard has returned three times. Also a plan that exhausted either critic's round bound before Green Light, or whose second critic produced no result twice, parked with `needs-human` and the finding still open (DRE-5268); a one-off card the pre-approval critic sent back `MAX_ROUNDS` times, or whose revision the planner did not finish, parked with `needs-human` and every finding named — a revision loop that does not converge is a defect, not a decision (DRE-5376); and a card that sat in Planning past that lane's window with nothing happening to it — the sweep's stall exit parks it in Triage with the reason on it and no label (DRE-4124 as amended by DRE-5268). Either critic bound reaches this lane only after it was first tried without a person (DRE-6452): the bound exit (`scripts/plan_bound.py`) reads the worst finding of every send-back round on the attempt, a decision-class finding goes to Green Light as one question, a revision-class set gets one more planner rewrite on a fresh attempt, once per card, and the park here comes only after that. Also a card the planning classifier could not read — its call came back with no classification and failed the same way on its one retry — parked by `planning_escalation.park_unread` with a note saying what happened, opening with the stall exit's tag, and no label (DRE-5975): nothing has read it, so there is nothing for the CEO to decide, and moving it back to Planning starts a fresh plan run. And one card for a stalled groom queue (DRE-5435): approved cards queued in Intake for a planner slot, a slot free, nothing released and nothing changing the queue for the planner line's own bound — the bureau-pipeline sweep CREATES that card in Triage, `no-code` and with no `agent:*` role, the whole notice in its body, and never a second while it is open. The queue is the pipeline's to unstick, not the CEO's to decide, so it is never sent to Green Light. And a card with no dispatch route — a `repo:<slug>` label that is not a key of `config/repo-map.json` — is parked here by the sweep's stranded watchdog with its reason stamped on it (`🔒 hold: reason=no-route`, DRE-6177); it is left alone by the hygiene agent's Triage lane while the hold stands, and is lifted by the hygiene agent's holds lane when the card's `repo:` label names a repo on the rail — corrected by a person, or newly joined (DRE-6172). Not live yet: the holds lane's lift lands with DRE-6180 and its return to Planning with DRE-6273; until then a person lifts the hold by clearing `needs-human` and moving the card to Planning.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2723 defines what may be parked here._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | Somebody fixes the card, and it re-enters at Intake. Triage is not a decision queue — a card waiting on the CEO belongs in Green Light. An operator re-enters a parked epic by clearing `needs-human` and moving it to Planning: a plan run fires for any card entering Planning, the route opens a fresh planning attempt, and the planner and both critics read the plan again (DRE-5268). The plan run that fires when an `agent:planner` card ENTERS Triage is refused by the plan-gate when the card carries `needs-human` or its newest comment is a `planning-stall-park` note, so a park stays parked until a person moves it (DRE-5277). Or the hygiene agent fixes the mechanical defect and returns the card to Backlog, never Todo (DRE-5365). The hygiene agent's holds lane lifts a hold whose condition has cleared and returns the card to the lane the pipeline resumes it in: a `no-route` hold to Planning when the card's `repo:` label now names a repo on the rail, so that Planning's exit routes it afresh, and a `fix-dispute` or `unfixable-check` hold to In Review when its open pull request has a new head (DRE-6172). Not live yet: the lifts land with DRE-6180 and the returns with DRE-6273; until then a person lifts such a hold by clearing `needs-human` and moving the card.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2723._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | Whatever found the defect: the relay, the sweep, either agent run, the planner parking a plan at either critic's bound (DRE-5268) or a one-off card at the one-off critic's bound (DRE-5376), or a human.  
Permitted writers: `relay`, `reconcile.py`, `plan.yml`, `agent-task.yml`, `agent-fix.yml`, `operator` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | The defect, named on the card by whatever bounced it.  
_Waiting on: DRE-2723._ | Phase 5 — promised |

### Canceled

| Clause | What it requires | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entrance** | A human decided the work will not be done — or, for a dependabot card, the pull request it was filed for closed unmerged (DRE-3665) — or, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal, the groomer's drain moved it with his reason written onto the card (DRE-4677). In all three a human decided; what differs is who wrote it down. Or, fourth, the card is a returned child of an epic that the planner split into sibling cards under the same epic, and it was canceled with those siblings named on it (DRE-5242): nothing is dropped, because every piece of the work is a sibling, and the original is canceled rather than Done because no code shipped. Or, fifth, the card's parent epic is itself Canceled or Duplicate and the hygiene agent canceled the child with the parent's state named on it (DRE-5365): the human decided on the parent, and the agent wrote the consequence down for a child that has no children of its own. Or, sixth, a build agent's `nothing-to-change` blocker attested every acceptance criterion of the card as already holding on the default branch, one checked line per criterion quoted on the card, and the sweep counted a checked line per criterion and canceled it (DRE-6458): no human decided this one. It is the pipeline's own act, narrowed to that one class, and it drops no work, because there was none to do — a person reverses it by reopening the card.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **exit** | None. Terminal.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| **writers** | A human — and two mechanisms, each for exactly one class, neither of them deciding anything. The sweep, for a card it filed for a dependabot pull request that then closed without merging (DRE-3665): dependabot superseding its own pull request, or a person closing it, is the decision; the sweep records it. The groomer's drain, for a card the CEO agreed to cancel on a groomer proposal (DRE-4677): the groomer proposes cancellations and the CEO agrees card by card in the console, and his per-card agree is the decision — the drain writes Canceled for exactly the cards on the approved proposal's Cancel table that he did not exclude, with the reason he read written onto each one as a comment. The principle the clause states is unchanged in both: a human decided. What changes is who writes it down. And the planner (plan.yml), for a returned child of an epic (DRE-5242): a card that came back to Planning, was read afresh as an epic, and is itself a child of an epic is split into sibling cards under that epic, and the planner run that filed them cancels the original with a comment naming every sibling — never Done, because no code shipped (standards/card-quality.md, How to split). That one is the pipeline's own act, narrowed to that one class, and it drops no work: every piece of the card lives on in a sibling carrying its own routing verdict. And the hygiene agent, for that one class only, a childless card under a Canceled or Duplicate parent, never deciding anything. And the sweep (reconcile.py), for a sixth class, a build agent's `nothing-to-change` blocker that attested every acceptance criterion, the agent's lines quoted on the card (DRE-6458): the agent attested every acceptance criterion as already holding on the default branch, one `- [x]` line per criterion, and the sweep counted a checked line per criterion against the card's own criteria before it wrote Canceled, conditional on the card still being in Backlog and unheld. No human decided this one. It is the pipeline's own act, narrowed to that one class, and it drops no work, because there was none to do — a person reverses it by reopening the card.  
Permitted writers: `operator`, `reconcile.py`, `groomer.py`, `plan.yml`, `hygiene.py` | Phase 2 — live |
| **evidence** | A human's decision, on the card.  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history Phase 5 records._ | Phase 5 — promised |

## The rules the harness asserts

| Rule | What it means | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `board.every_state_is_named` | No state exists in Linear that the contract does not name.  
_A leftover design-review state sat on the board with one card ever and zero code references, and nobody noticed for four months (DRE-2726 retired it; DRE-2818 deleted the last entry naming it)._ | Phase 2 — live |
| `board.every_lane_exists` | No lane is named that does not exist in Linear.  
_The other half of the same pair: a contract that names a lane the board dropped is a contract nothing can satisfy._ | Phase 2 — live |
| `board.retiring_lane_is_empty` | A retiring lane holds no cards.  
_A lane the pipeline no longer writes to is a lane nothing will move a card out of. An occupied one is a stranded card._  
_Waiting on: Phase 3 is when the wave asserts it. Nothing is retiring today (DRE-2818 deleted the last two entries once Linear archived their states), so the clause is vacuously satisfied and skipped; it earns its keep on the NEXT retirement, where the sweep's drain (reconcile.drain_retiring_lanes) empties the lane and this is what proves the drain finished._ | Phase 3 — promised |
| `board.retired_entry_is_deleted` | A retiring entry whose Linear state is already gone is deleted from this file.  
_A retirement that never finishes is drift too. Once the board catches up, the entry is the last copy of a lane that no longer exists._ | Phase 2 — live |
| `console.state_lists_carry_every_lane` | Every lane the pipeline knows appears in the console's state lists, and the console names no state the contract does not carry.  
_The console's vocabulary carried Proposed and HOLD, neither of which is a Linear state, and it renders an Intake column that can never fill._ | Phase 2 — live |
| `pipeline.vocabulary_is_contract_lanes` | The pipeline's own scripts and workflows name no state the contract does not carry.  
_A workflow that advances a card into an archived state fails its Linear call at 2am, on a card nobody is watching._ | Phase 2 — live |
| `transition.permitted_writer` | Every transition observed was made by a writer the destination lane permits.  
_A lane's writer list is only a contract if something reads the transition log against it._  
_Waiting on: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records._ | Phase 5 — promised |
| `transition.required_evidence` | Every transition observed carried the evidence the destination lane requires.  
_The evidence clause is the one that makes occupancy justifiable rather than assumed._  
_Waiting on: the routing verdict exists and is readable (DRE-2724); still needed is the plan artifact gate (DRE-2720) and a writer that stamps every card at planning exit (DRE-2721)._ | Phase 5 — promised |
